jobs.title: Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
About Kinaxis

Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you!

In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today.

Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers.

Location

Ottawa and Toronto, CA - Hybrid

Other Canadian locations - Remote

About The Team

Our Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) team partners with leaders across the company to help drive business decisions. They work with stakeholders to highlight insights and analysis needed to make data-driven decisions that help fuel growth and operational excellence. The Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, is a trusted advisor and subject matter expert who brings a depth and breadth of knowledge and expertise in leading, directing, and developing the overall operations and delivery of revenue forecasting, consolidated forecasts and reporting, external metrics, and evolving financial planning strategies within Kinaxis.

This role is ideal for a forward-thinking finance leader who combines deep financial expertise with strong business acumen, operational excellence, and a passion for transforming finance through data, automation, and AI-enabled insights.

Partnering closely with the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis the Director, Financial Planning & Analysis is responsible for effective management and continuous improvement of budgeting and forecasting cycles and provides strategic financial consultation and support to the business.

Vacancy Status

This is an existing job vacancy

What you will do

Business Performance & FP&A Excellence

Build an integrated, enterprise-wide planning process across business units and regions to drive business objectives and long-term growth.
Develop key financial models and scenarios to evaluate strategic initiatives and investments, with a view to multi-year projections.
Lead scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and financial modeling to support strategic decisions.
Manage and drive management reporting – analyze financial results, distill and synthesize issues and communicate key messages (including business risks) to the senior leadership team.
Support Board reporting, executive presentations, and investor reporting and communications.
Deliver actionable financial insights that influence investment priorities, resource allocation, pricing, and growth initiatives.
Demonstrated outstanding communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear business insights.
Develop KPIs and performance dashboards that provide timely visibility into business health.
Foster strong partnerships across the organization including Product, Sales, Corporate Functions and other teams.

Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize FP&A through automation, AI-enabled analytics, and scalable planning technologies.
Propose and implement continuous improvement of strategies, processes, systems, and policies to enhance the speed and effectiveness of forecasting and reporting.
Establish best-in-class planning processes, governance, and data quality.
Champion the use of modern planning platforms and business intelligence tools.

Leadership

Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing global FP&A organization.
Create a culture of accountability, curiosity, continuous improvement, and business partnership.
Lead organizational change and finance transformation initiatives across a global business, including exploring additional areas to implement AI initiatives.

What we are looking for

Post-secondary education in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field.
Professional accounting designation(CPA or legacy CA, CMA or CGA), CFA, or MBA.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, investment banking, private equity, or corporate finance, ideally with some experience in a high-tech, global, publicly traded organization.
Experience leading teams with direct and indirect reports.
Demonstrated financial acumen and expertise in data and financial modeling and scenario planning.
Advanced analytical, problem solving, and critical-thinking skills with the ability to coordinate input from multiple sources to develop impactful recommendations to achieve results for the business.
An articulate and professional communicator with the ability to provide clear, concise messaging to multiple audiences and present complex information across the organization.
Strong relationship-building and influencing skills and the ability to prioritize business requirements appropriately through a collaborative partnership approach.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate input from multiple complex sources, conduct environmental scanning, and sort through ambiguity to develop impactful recommendations for business decisions.
Deep and broad knowledge of financial analysis, forecasting, budgeting, and management reporting, including oversight of the annual financial planning process and related best practices.
Exceptional financial modelling skills with great attention to detail and the ability to distill complex issues into structured, actionable frameworks.
Highly proficient in Excel and PowerPoint, particularly for financial modeling, financial and data analysis, and presenting business cases or transaction summaries.
Ability to apply a structured problem-solving framework to ambiguous situations and drive decisions under tight timelines.
Significant experience developing business cases supported by financial analysis and modeling, with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally across the organization.

#Director

Work With Impact:
Our platform directly helps companies power the world’s supply chains. We see the results of what we do out in the world every day, when we see store shelves stocked, when medications are available for our loved ones, and so much more.

Work with Fortune 500 Brands:
Companies across industries trust us to help them take control of their integrated business planning and digital supply chain. Some of our customers include Lockheed Martin, Unilever, P&G, ExxonMobil, Cisco and more.

Social Responsibility at Kinaxis:
Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Committee weighs in on hiring practices, talent assessment training materials, and mandatory training on unconscious bias and inclusion fundamentals. Sustainability is key to what we do and we’re committed to a long-term net-zero operations strategy. We are involved in our communities and support causes where we can make the most impact.

People matter at Kinaxis and here are some of the perks and benefits we offer, which may vary by location and employee:

Flexible vacation and Kinaxis Days (company-wide days off)
Flexible work options
Physical and mental well-being programs
Regularly scheduled virtual fitness classes
Mentorship programs, training, and career development
Recognition programs and referral rewards
Hackathons

For more information, visit the Kinaxis website at www.kinaxis.com or the company’s blog at http://blog.kinaxis.com .

Kinaxis welcomes candidates to apply to our inclusive community. We provide accommodations upon request to ensure fairness and accessibility throughout our recruitment process for all candidates, including those with specific needs or disabilities. If you require an accommodation, please reach out to us at recruitmentprograms@kinaxis.com. This contact information is for accessibility requests only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications.

Kinaxis is committed to ensuring a fair and transparent recruitment process. We use artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the initial step of the recruitment process to compare submitted resumes against the job description to identify candidates whose education, experience, and skills most closely match the requirements of the role. After the initial screening, all subsequent decisions regarding your application, including final selection, are made by our human recruitment team. AI does not make any final hiring decisions.

jobs.title: Finance Director, Canada
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

At Nexans our global vision is to electrify the future. For over a century, Nexans has played a crucial role in the electrification of the planet. With around 28,000 people in 42 countries, the Group is leading the charge to the new world of electrification: safer, sustainable, renewable, decarbonized and accessible to everyone Nexans recognizes the differences that make each employee valuable and unique.

WELCOMING YOU TO THE TEAM

Our story starts in 1911, manufacturing cables to support the distribution of power generated from Niagara Falls, Nexans has proudly contributed to Canada's growth. We have been involved in many of Canada's most ambitious projects; from dams, bridges, energy transmission and distribution to railroads and transportation. We are a vertically integrated manufacturer and our products are made at facilities located in Quebec, Ontario, and Saskatchewan.

As Finance Director, Canada, you will report directly to the VP Finance, North America. This role is being created as part of the North American transformation, establishing dedicated Canadian and US organizations under a new North American business group. The Finance Director will provide financial leadership for the Canadian business, partnering closely with the broader North American leadership team to drive financial performance and support the growth and development of the Canadian organization

GETTING TO KNOW THE POSITION

One of the strategic orientations that Nexans pursues consists in capturing growth and differentiating its offer by escalading the value chain from the production of cables towards the provision of innovative cable systems and services and solutions to better address the current and future needs of our partners and customers.

The Finance Director, Canada is responsible for driving the financial performance of the Canadian Business Unit in alignment with NAM objectives. The role oversees financial planning, budgeting, reporting, and controls, while ensuring compliance with Group policies and supporting sound business decisions. The Finance Director also leads and develops the Canadian finance team, partnering with the business to optimize financial performance and resources.

How You Make An Impact

Financial Strategy & Business Performance

Directs and oversees the financial activities of the Canadian organization, ensuring strong financial performance, sound governance, and alignment with Nexans Group and North American objectives.
Provides strategic financial leadership and insight to support business decisions, including investments, acquisitions, divestitures, capital allocation, pension matters, and other strategic initiatives.
Provides timely and accurate financial analysis, reporting, forecasts, and business indicators to support decision-making by Canadian and North American senior management, Nexans Corporate, and COMEX.
Acts as a strategic business partner to the leadership team and operational functions, providing financial expertise and challenging assumptions to support profitable and sustainable growth.
Monitors business and market trends, including relevant competitor and economic developments, and provides financial insights to support the organization's positioning and decision-making.
Provides financial advice and support in the negotiation and review of strategic commercial contracts and agreements, including contracts with significant financial, commodity, or foreign exchange exposure.

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Leads the annual budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes, ensuring alignment with business objectives and Group requirements.
Continually improves the budgeting and forecasting process by strengthening financial discipline and developing the financial understanding of department and business leaders.
Oversees the monitoring of financial performance against budget, forecast, and business objectives, identifying risks, opportunities, and corrective actions.
Provides financial analysis and recommendations to support cost optimization and improve overall business performance.

Financial Reporting & Governance

Defines and oversees the monthly consolidated reporting process, including sales, P&L, MMR, and other key financial indicators for the Canadian organization and North American Business Group.
Ensures the timely and accurate preparation and consolidation of financial reports, management analysis, forecasts, and financial outlooks.
Ensures compliance with applicable accounting standards, Group policies, IFRS, and Canadian accounting and regulatory requirements.
Establishes, implements, and maintains appropriate financial policies, procedures, systems, and internal controls to safeguard company assets and ensure the integrity and reliability of financial information.
Represents Finance in internal and external audits and ensures timely follow-up and resolution of audit findings.

Cash, Treasury, Tax & Risk Management

Develops and implements strategies to optimize cash flow, working capital, liquidity, and overall financial performance.
Oversees treasury activities, banking relationships, credit policies, and other areas impacting the organization's cash position and financial resilience.
Ensures, in coordination with Nexans Corporate and relevant internal stakeholders, compliance with applicable Canadian tax requirements and monitors changes in legislation that may impact the business.
Identifies, assesses, and manages key financial and business risks, ensuring appropriate mitigation measures and controls are in place.
Provides financial guidance on matters involving foreign exchange, commodity exposure, financing, and other financial risks, as applicable.

Finance Transformation & Continuous Improvement

Leads initiatives to optimize financial processes, strengthen cost control, improve reporting efficiency, and increase the automation and digitalization of Finance activities.
Drives continuous improvement of Finance systems, processes, and controls to improve the overall efficiency, effectiveness, and quality of financial operations.
Ensures that Finance policies, procedures, and systems evolve in line with the organization's changing business needs and Group requirements.

Finance Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness

Leads and develops the Finance organization, ensuring appropriate capabilities, performance, succession, and professional development to support the organization's financial objectives.
Continuously assesses the effectiveness and organizational structure of the Finance function and implements improvements to enhance efficiency and business support.
Promotes a strong culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, compliance, and business partnership within the Finance organization.

North American & Group Collaboration

Supports and contributes to North American strategic initiatives and synergies, including cross-functional initiatives defined as NAM priorities.
Collaborates closely with Nexans Corporate, North American leadership, and other Finance leaders to ensure alignment of financial strategies, reporting, controls, and business priorities.
Provides financial support and analysis for major North American and Group initiatives, ensuring appropriate financial evaluation, risk assessment, and follow-up.
Ensures effective communication of financial performance, risks, opportunities, and recommendations to senior leadership and relevant stakeholders.

You will be expected to:

Maximize the Canadian BU profits through an adequate administration of expenses, costs, placement of funds and use of resources.
Deliver accurate and timely financial reporting, forecasts, and insights to support business decisions.
Improve financial performance through strong planning, cost control, and working capital management.
Ensure compliance with Nexans policies, accounting standards, internal controls, and Canadian regulations.
Build a strong and effective Finance team with the right capabilities to support the business.
Drive continuous improvement and strengthen Finance processes, systems, and business support.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE ?

Key Competencies & Requirements

Professional degree in Accounting and/or related fields
Postgraduate degree / Master Finance or MBA
Minimum 7 years of experience directing financial areas, or developing financial processes
Knowledge of IFRS accounting standards
Knowledge in the SAP/BI System
Financial reporting/consolidation

Type of Position: New position

Use of AI: None

Salary: [$170,000.00 per annum to $185,000.00 Per annum]

Requests for accommodation due to a disability (which may be visible or invisible, temporary or permanent) can be made at any stage of application and employment. We encourage candidates to make their accommodation needs known so that we can provide equitable opportunities.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Strategic Business Executive
jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

________________________________________

Procurement Governance

Establish financial oversight and governance for procurement activities.
Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

________________________________________

Indigenous Relations & Partnership Development

Build and maintain respectful relationships with Tsuut'ina Nation leadership and stakeholders.
Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

________________________________________

Stakeholder Management

The CFO Will Maintain Productive Relationships With

Internal Stakeholders

Board of Directors
Executive Leadership Team
Department Leaders
Team Members

External Stakeholders

Tsuut'ina Nation Leadership
Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC)
Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC)
Auditors
Financial Institutions
Legal Counsel
Development Partners
Government Agencies
Industry Associations
Consultants and Contractors

________________________________________

Risk Management & Governance

Lead enterprise risk management activities.
Ensure effective internal controls and compliance programs.
Support Board governance and Finance & Audit Committee activities.
Oversee annual external audits.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and accounting standards.
Develop financial risk mitigation strategies.

________________________________________

BOARD FINANCE & AUDIT COMMITTEE SUPPORT

The CFO serves as management's primary liaison to the Finance and Audit Committee and is responsible for:

Preparing committee materials and recommendations.
Presenting financial results and forecasts.
Supporting audit processes.
Monitoring risk management activities.
Reporting on compliance and internal controls.
Supporting governance best practices.

________________________________________

We thank all applicants, however, only those considered for an interview will be contacted.No phone calls please.

Priority will be given to Tsuut'ina Nation members.

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Strategic Business Executive
new_jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

________________________________________

Procurement Governance

Establish financial oversight and governance for procurement activities.
Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

________________________________________

Indigenous Relations & Partnership Development

Build and maintain respectful relationships with Tsuut'ina Nation leadership and stakeholders.
Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

________________________________________

Stakeholder Management

The CFO Will Maintain Productive Relationships With

Internal Stakeholders

Board of Directors
Executive Leadership Team
Department Leaders
Team Members

External Stakeholders

Tsuut'ina Nation Leadership
Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC)
Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC)
Auditors
Financial Institutions
Legal Counsel
Development Partners
Government Agencies
Industry Associations
Consultants and Contractors

________________________________________

Risk Management & Governance

Lead enterprise risk management activities.
Ensure effective internal controls and compliance programs.
Support Board governance and Finance & Audit Committee activities.
Oversee annual external audits.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and accounting standards.
Develop financial risk mitigation strategies.

________________________________________

BOARD FINANCE & AUDIT COMMITTEE SUPPORT

The CFO serves as management's primary liaison to the Finance and Audit Committee and is responsible for:

Preparing committee materials and recommendations.
Presenting financial results and forecasts.
Supporting audit processes.
Monitoring risk management activities.
Reporting on compliance and internal controls.
Supporting governance best practices.

________________________________________

We thank all applicants, however, only those considered for an interview will be contacted.No phone calls please.

Priority will be given to Tsuut'ina Nation members.
